stem: Find the area of the sector of a circle with radius 4 cm and of angle \(30^\circ\). Also, find the area of the corresponding major sector. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
solution:
Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2\)

\(= \dfrac{30}{360} \times 3.14 \times 4 \times 4\ \text{cm}^2\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{12} \times 3.14 \times 16 = \dfrac{12.56}{3} = 4.19\ \text{cm}^2\) (approx.)

Area of the corresponding major sector

\(= \pi r^2 - \text{area of the minor sector}\)

\(= (3.14 \times 16 - 4.19)\ \text{cm}^2 = 50.24 - 4.19 = 46.05\ \text{cm}^2\)

Alternatively, area of the major sector \(= \dfrac{360 - 30}{360} \times \pi r^2 = \dfrac{330}{360} \times 3.14 \times 16 = 46.05\ \text{cm}^2\).

stem: Find the area of the segment AYB shown in Fig. 11.6, if the radius of the circle is 21 cm and \(\angle\)AOB \(= 120^\circ\). (Use \(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\))
solution:
Area of the segment AYB \(= \) Area of sector OAYB \(-\) Area of \(\triangle\)OAB  ... (1)

Now, area of the sector OAYB \(= \dfrac{120}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 21\ \text{cm}^2 = 462\ \text{cm}^2\)  ... (2)

For the area of \(\triangle\)OAB, draw OM \(\perp\) AB.

Since OA \(=\) OB, by RHS congruence \(\triangle\)AMO \(\cong\) \(\triangle\)BMO, so M bisects AB and \(\angle\)AOM \(=\) \(\angle\)BOM \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 120^\circ = 60^\circ\).

So \(\dfrac{\text{OM}}{\text{OA}} = \cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\), giving \(\text{OM} = \dfrac{21}{2}\) cm,

and \(\dfrac{\text{AM}}{\text{OA}} = \sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), giving \(\text{AM} = \dfrac{21\sqrt{3}}{2}\) cm, so \(\text{AB} = 21\sqrt{3}\) cm.

So, area of \(\triangle\)OAB \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{AB} \times \text{OM} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 21\sqrt{3} \times \dfrac{21}{2} = \dfrac{441\sqrt{3}}{4}\ \text{cm}^2\)  ... (3)

Therefore, from (1), (2) and (3),

area of the segment AYB \(= \left(462 - \dfrac{441\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)\text{cm}^2 = \dfrac{21}{4}\left(88 - 21\sqrt{3}\right)\text{cm}^2\).

stem: Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm if angle of the sector is \(60^\circ\).
solution:
Area of a sector \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2\)

\(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 6 \times 6 = \dfrac{1}{6} \times \dfrac{22 \times 36}{7} = \dfrac{132}{7}\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: Find the area of a quadrant of a circle whose circumference is 22 cm.
solution:
Circumference \(= 2\pi r = 22\), so \(2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times r = 22\), giving \(r = \dfrac{7}{2}\) cm.

A quadrant is a sector of angle \(90^\circ\):

Area \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{49}{4} = \dfrac{77}{8}\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: The length of the minute hand of a clock is 14 cm. Find the area swept by the minute hand in 5 minutes.
solution:
In 60 minutes the minute hand sweeps \(360^\circ\), so in 5 minutes it sweeps \(\dfrac{5}{60} \times 360^\circ = 30^\circ\).

Area swept \(= \dfrac{30}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 14 \times 14 = \dfrac{1}{12} \times \dfrac{22 \times 196}{7} = \dfrac{154}{3}\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: A chord of a circle of radius 15 cm subtends an angle of \(60^\circ\) at the centre. Find the areas of the corresponding minor and major segments of the circle. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\) and \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
solution:
Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times 3.14 \times 15 \times 15 = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 706.5 = 117.75\ \text{cm}^2\)

Since the angle at the centre is \(60^\circ\) and the two radii are equal, the triangle is EQUILATERAL with side 15 cm:

Area of the triangle \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 15^2 = \dfrac{1.73}{4} \times 225 = 97.3125\ \text{cm}^2\)

Minor segment \(= 117.75 - 97.3125 = 20.4375\ \text{cm}^2\)

Area of the circle \(= 3.14 \times 225 = 706.5\ \text{cm}^2\)

Major segment \(= 706.5 - 20.4375 = 686.0625\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: A chord of a circle of radius 12 cm subtends an angle of \(120^\circ\) at the centre. Find the area of the corresponding segment of the circle. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\) and \(\sqrt{3} = 1.73\))
solution:
Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{120}{360} \times 3.14 \times 12 \times 12 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 452.16 = 150.72\ \text{cm}^2\)

The triangle has two sides 12 cm with \(120^\circ\) between them, so

Area of the triangle \(= \dfrac{1}{2} r^2 \sin 120^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 144 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 36\sqrt{3} = 36 \times 1.73 = 62.28\ \text{cm}^2\)

Area of the segment \(= 150.72 - 62.28 = 88.44\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: An umbrella has 8 ribs which are equally spaced (see Fig. 11.10). Assuming umbrella to be a flat circle of radius 45 cm, find the area between the two consecutive ribs of the umbrella.
solution:
The 8 ribs divide the circle into 8 equal sectors, so each sector has angle \(\dfrac{360^\circ}{8} = 45^\circ\).

Area between two consecutive ribs \(= \dfrac{1}{8} \times \pi r^2 = \dfrac{1}{8} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 45 \times 45\)

\(= \dfrac{22 \times 2025}{56} = \dfrac{22275}{28}\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: A car has two wipers which do not overlap. Each wiper has a blade of length 25 cm sweeping through an angle of \(115^\circ\). Find the total area cleaned at each sweep of the blades.
solution:
Each blade sweeps a sector of radius 25 cm and angle \(115^\circ\):

Area of one sector \(= \dfrac{115}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 25 \times 25 = \dfrac{115 \times 22 \times 625}{2520} = \dfrac{158125}{252}\ \text{cm}^2\)

Since the wipers do not overlap, the total area cleaned is twice this:

Total area \(= 2 \times \dfrac{158125}{252} = \dfrac{158125}{126}\ \text{cm}^2\)

stem: To warn ships for underwater rocks, a lighthouse spreads a red coloured light over a sector of angle \(80^\circ\) to a distance of 16.5 km. Find the area of the sea over which the ships are warned. (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
solution:
Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{80}{360} \times 3.14 \times (16.5)^2\)

\(= \dfrac{2}{9} \times 3.14 \times 272.25 = \dfrac{2}{9} \times 854.865\)

\(= 189.97\ \text{km}^2\)

stem: A round table cover has six equal designs as shown in Fig. 11.11. If the radius of the cover is 28 cm, find the cost of making the designs at the rate of ₹ 0.35 per cm\(^2\). (Use \(\sqrt{3} = 1.7\))
solution:
The six designs are the six segments left outside a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle, so each subtends \(\dfrac{360^\circ}{6} = 60^\circ\) at the centre.

Area of one sector \(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 28 \times 28 = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 2464 = \dfrac{1232}{3}\ \text{cm}^2\)

The triangle is equilateral with side 28 cm:

Area of the triangle \(= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \times 28^2 = \dfrac{1.7}{4} \times 784 = 333.2\ \text{cm}^2\)

Area of one design \(= \dfrac{1232}{3} - 333.2 = 410.6\overline{6} - 333.2 = \dfrac{1162}{15}\ \text{cm}^2\)

Area of all six designs \(= 6 \times \dfrac{1162}{15} = \dfrac{2324}{5} = 464.8\ \text{cm}^2\)

Cost \(= 464.8 \times 0.35 = \) ₹ 162.68

solution:

stem: the length of the arc
solution:
Length of an arc \(= \dfrac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2\pi r\)

\(= \dfrac{60}{360} \times 2 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 132 = 22\ \text{cm}\)

A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m long rope (see Fig. 11.8). Find (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
stem: the area of that part of the field in which the horse can graze.
solution:
The peg is at a CORNER of the square, so the horse can sweep a quarter circle of radius 5 m (the field's two sides block the rest).

Area \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 3.14 \times 5 \times 5 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 78.5 = 19.625\ \text{m}^2\)

A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square shaped grass field of side 15 m by means of a 5 m long rope (see Fig. 11.8). Find (Use \(\pi = 3.14\))
stem: the increase in the grazing area if the rope were 10 m long instead of 5 m.
solution:
With a 10 m rope the horse sweeps a quarter circle of radius 10 m. Since the field's side is 15 m, the quarter circle still fits inside it.

Area \(= \dfrac{90}{360} \times 3.14 \times 10 \times 10 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 314 = 78.5\ \text{m}^2\)

Increase \(= 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875\ \text{m}^2\)

[Textbook: the answer key prints this as \(58.875\ \text{cm}^2\). The VALUE is right; the UNIT is not. The field is 15 m square and the ropes are 5 m and 10 m, so the increase can only be in square METRES.]

A brooch is made with silver wire in the form of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also used in making 5 diameters which divide the circle into 10 equal sectors as shown in Fig. 11.9. Find :
stem: the total length of the silver wire required.
solution:
The wire forms the circumference plus the 5 diameters.

Circumference \(= \pi d = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 35 = 110\) mm

Five diameters \(= 5 \times 35 = 175\) mm

Total length \(= 110 + 175 = 285\) mm

A brooch is made with silver wire in the form of a circle with diameter 35 mm. The wire is also used in making 5 diameters which divide the circle into 10 equal sectors as shown in Fig. 11.9. Find :
stem: the area of each sector of the brooch.
solution:
The radius is \(\dfrac{35}{2}\) mm, and the 10 sectors are equal, so each is one tenth of the circle.

Area of each sector \(= \dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \left(\dfrac{35}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times \dfrac{1225}{4}\)

\(= \dfrac{1}{10} \times \dfrac{26950}{28} = \dfrac{385}{4}\ \text{mm}^2\)

stem: Tick the correct answer in the following : Area of a sector of angle \(p\) (in degrees) of a circle with radius R is
solution:
The area of a sector of angle \(p\) is \(\dfrac{p}{360} \times \pi \text{R}^2\).

Check each option:

- (A) \(\dfrac{p}{180} \times 2\pi\text{R}\) has the dimensions of a LENGTH, not an area.
- (B) \(\dfrac{p}{180} \times \pi\text{R}^2\) is twice the correct value.
- (C) \(\dfrac{p}{360} \times 2\pi\text{R}\) is the arc LENGTH, not the area.
- (D) \(\dfrac{p}{720} \times 2\pi\text{R}^2 = \dfrac{2p}{720} \times \pi\text{R}^2 = \dfrac{p}{360} \times \pi\text{R}^2\). **Correct.**

So the answer is **(D)**.
